quick: Start 12.5 mg once/twice daily; usual 300-450 mg/day
Use only if clearly needed; monitor neonate
Caution; consider lower dose in significant impairment
ANC (weekly initially), weight, glucose, lipids, ECG
summary: Clozapine is an atypical antipsychotic reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and for reducing recurrent suicidal behavior in schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder. Because of severe neutropenia it requires REMS-mandated ANC monitoring. Boxed warnings cover severe neutropenia, orthostatic hypotension/bradycardia/syncope, seizure, myocarditis/cardiomyopathy, and increased mortality in elderly dementia patients. Started low at 12.5 mg and titrated slowly to 300-450 mg/day.
indications: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (failure to respond adequately to standard antipsychotics)
Reduction of recurrent suicidal behavior in patients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder at chronic risk

dosage.n: Obtain baseline ANC >=1500/uL before starting (>=1000 if BEN)

dosage.d: Increase by 25-50 mg/day to 300-450 mg/day by end of 2 weeks
dosage.n: Then increase by up to 100 mg once or twice weekly

dosage.d: Restart at 12.5 mg once or twice daily
dosage.n: Risk of orthostatic hypotension/collapse on re-initiation

admin: Take orally with or without food; ODT may disintegrate or be chewed, no water needed
Always start at 12.5 mg and titrate slowly to limit orthostatic hypotension and seizures
Confirm baseline and ongoing ANC per Clozapine REMS schedule before dispensing
Do not abruptly discontinue; taper over 1-2 weeks unless neutropenia or other urgent reaction
Adjust dose for strong CYP1A2 inhibitors and for smoking cessation/initiation
moa: Antagonist at dopamine D1-D4 receptors with relatively low D2 occupancy, and potent antagonism at serotonin 5-HT2A, alpha-adrenergic, histamine H1, and muscarinic receptors. The high 5-HT2A to D2 blockade ratio and limbic-selective dopamine action are thought to explain efficacy in treatment-resistant disease with low extrapyramidal liability.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to clozapine (e.g. photosensitivity, vasculitis, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
relative: History of severe neutropenia or myeloproliferative disorder
Significant cardiac disease / paralytic ileus / severe GI hypomotility
monitor: Glucose, lipids and weight for metabolic effects

preg: Third-trimester exposure may cause neonatal extrapyramidal and withdrawal symptoms. Use only if potential benefit justifies risk; there is a pregnancy exposure registry for antipsychotics. Monitor neonate for sedation, feeding difficulty and abnormal muscle movements.
lact: Clozapine is present in breast milk; breastfeeding is not recommended due to risk of sedation, agranulocytosis and seizures in the infant.
renal: Use with caution in significant renal impairment; consider a reduced dose and slower titration. No formal dose adjustment defined in mild impairment.
hepatic: Use caution in hepatic impairment; reduce dose and monitor liver enzymes. Discontinue if hepatitis or transaminase elevations with systemic symptoms develop.

major: Strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin) - markedly raise clozapine levels; reduce dose
Other myelosuppressive agents (carbamazepine, chemotherapy) - additive neutropenia risk; avoid
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, phenytoin) and smoking - reduce clozapine levels
minor: Caffeine - modest increase in clozapine levels
Valproate - variable effect on clozapine concentration
interactions.food: Caffeine may modestly raise levels; effect is generally minor.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; additive sedation and CNS/respiratory depression.
interactions.diagnostics: Can lower ANC/WBC, elevate eosinophils, glucose, lipids and liver enzymes; may prolong QTc.

monitoring: Absolute neutrophil count per Clozapine REMS (weekly x6 months, then q2 weeks x6 months, then monthly)
Weight, BMI, fasting glucose/HbA1c and lipids at baseline and periodically
Blood pressure and heart rate during titration; ECG/QTc if cardiac risk
Troponin/CRP and echocardiography if myocarditis suspected (especially first 2 months)
Bowel function and constipation; liver enzymes if symptomatic
counsel: Attend all blood tests; clozapine cannot be dispensed without an in-range ANC
Report fever, sore throat or signs of infection immediately
Report chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, fainting or persistent constipation
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially early in treatment
Do not stop suddenly; tell your prescriber if you start or stop smoking (affects levels)
pk: Antipsychotic effect over days to weeks
Steady state in ~1 week with twice-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect ODT from moisture
pearls: Reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia after >=2 adequate antipsychotic trials
Only antipsychotic with an indication to reduce recurrent suicidal behavior
Boxed warnings: severe neutropenia, orthostasis/bradycardia/syncope, seizure, myocarditis/cardiomyopathy, increased mortality in elderly dementia psychosis
Smoking induces CYP1A2 - stopping smoking can sharply raise clozapine levels and toxicity
Hypersalivation and constipation are common and constipation can progress to life-threatening ileus
missed: If a dose is missed take it when remembered unless near the next dose; do not double up. If clozapine has been stopped for 2 or more days, do NOT resume the previous dose - contact the prescriber to re-titrate from 12.5 mg.
overdose: Manifestations include altered consciousness, hypersalivation, tachycardia, hypotension, respiratory depression, seizures and coma. There is no specific antidote; provide airway support, cardiac and respiratory monitoring, activated charcoal if early, and treat hypotension and arrhythmias. Avoid adrenaline (epinephrine) for hypotension due to possible paradoxical effect.
